name: Primary Bone Dysplasia with Micromelia

criteria.description: Presence of disproportionate shortening of the limbs (micromelia) evident at birth
Characteristic radiographic findings including abnormal bone morphology and metaphyseal irregularities
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with primary bone dysplasia
Postnatal growth retardation with disproportionate short stature

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of disproportionate micromelia with characteristic radiographic abnormalities; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing aids in confirmation and subclassification.

searchTerms: uneven body proportions with short height
short stature with abnormal body ratio

common.symptomName: Joint stiffness and limited range of motion
Delayed motor milestones due to skeletal abnormalities
searchTerms: slow motor skill development due to bone problems
late crawling or walking from skeletal issues

occasional.symptomName: Spinal deformities including scoliosis or kyphosis
Mild joint pain secondary to skeletal abnormalities
Mild respiratory compromise due to thoracic cage abnormalities
searchTerms: mild respiratory issues due to rib cage

rare.symptomName: Hearing impairment due to ossicular chain malformations
searchTerms: hearing loss from ear bone chain problems
middle ear bone defects causing hearing issues

rare.symptomName: Neurological complications secondary to spinal deformities
Cardiovascular anomalies associated with skeletal dysplasia
searchTerms: heart and vessel abnormalities with bone disease
cardiovascular problems linked to skeletal issues

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biochemical markers identified
imaging: Radiographs showing disproportionate shortening of long bones with metaphyseal irregularities
Spinal X-rays revealing scoliosis or kyphosis
Thoracic cage abnormalities on chest imaging
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes related to bone growth and development (e.g., FGFR3, COL2A1) may be identified
other: Prenatal ultrasound may detect limb shortening and skeletal abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Rhizomelic limb shortening rather than micromelia
Characteristic facial features such as frontal bossing
Milder limb shortening with less pronounced metaphyseal changes
Later onset and milder clinical presentation
Severe micromelia with cloverleaf skull deformity
Distinct radiographic features and FGFR3 mutations

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress due to thoracic cage hypoplasia
Progressive neurological deficits from spinal cord compression
Rapidly worsening skeletal deformities impairing mobility
references: Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders: 2019 revision. Am J Med Genet A. 2019.
Orphanet: Primary bone dysplasia with micromelia. ORPHA364536.

Warman ML, Cormier-Daire V, Hall C, Krakow D, Lachman R, LeMerrer M, Mortier G, Rimoin DL, Savarirayan R, Sillence D, Superti-Furga A. Nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders: 2010 revision. Am J Med Genet A. 2011.
